framework: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) as amended by CPRA
version: Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.100 et seq. + CCR Title 11 regulations
source_note: California Civil Code Title 1.81.5 as posted by the California Privacy Protection Agency (cppa.ca.gov, January 2025 update), plus Civil Code 1798.81.5 / 1798.82 and the CCPA regulations (CCR Title 11). Section numbers verified against it; the statute has no official section titles, so names are short descriptions.

sections.name: Duty to maintain reasonable security procedures
sections.description: Businesses owning/licensing personal information must use reasonable security practices to protect it from unauthorized access, destruction, use, modification or disclosure.

sections.name: Breach notification
sections.description: Disclose a breach of unencrypted personal information to affected California residents in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay.

sections.name: General duties / right to know; reasonable security
sections.description: Consumers' right to know; businesses must implement reasonable security procedures appropriate to the information (1798.100(e)).

sections.name: Right to delete
sections.description: Consumers may request deletion of personal information collected about them.

sections.name: Right to correct
sections.description: Consumers may request correction of inaccurate personal information.

sections.name: Right to know what personal information is collected; right to access
sections.description: Consumers may request the categories and specific pieces of personal information collected about them.

sections.name: Right to know what personal information is sold or shared, and to whom
sections.description: Consumers may request the categories sold or shared and the categories of third parties.

sections.name: Right to opt out of sale/sharing
sections.description: Consumers may direct a business not to sell or share their personal information.

sections.name: Right to limit use of sensitive personal information
sections.description: Consumers may limit the use and disclosure of sensitive personal information.

sections.name: Right of no retaliation following opt-out or exercise of other rights
sections.description: Businesses may not discriminate against consumers for exercising their rights; rules for financial incentives.

sections.name: Notice, disclosure, correction and deletion requirements
sections.description: Methods for submitting requests, 45-day response period, verification and privacy-policy disclosures.

sections.name: Methods of limiting sale, sharing and use of personal information
sections.description: "Do Not Sell or Share" and "Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information" links and opt-out preference signals.

sections.name: Definitions
sections.description: Statutory definitions (personal information, sale, sharing, business, service provider, contractor, etc.).

sections.name: Definition — sensitive personal information
sections.description: Includes government IDs, financial account + access credentials, precise geolocation, health, and similar.

sections.name: Definition — service provider
sections.description: A person that processes personal information on behalf of a business under a written contract.

sections.name: Exemptions
sections.description: Exemptions, e.g. compliance with law, legal claims, deidentified and aggregate information.

sections.name: Exemption for medical information and HIPAA-covered protected health information
sections.description: The title does not apply to medical information under the CMIA or PHI collected by HIPAA covered entities or business associates.

sections.name: Prohibition on reidentifying deidentified patient information
sections.description: Reidentifying information deidentified under HIPAA is prohibited except for listed purposes.

sections.name: Private right of action (data breach)
sections.description: Consumers may sue for statutory damages when nonencrypted/nonredacted personal information is subject to unauthorized access due to failure to maintain reasonable security.

sections.name: Administrative enforcement
sections.description: Administrative fines of up to $2,500 per violation, or $7,500 for intentional violations or those involving minors.

sections.name: Consumer Privacy Fund
sections.description: Fines and settlements are deposited in the Consumer Privacy Fund.

sections.name: Conflicting provisions
sections.description: The title is supplemental; in conflict, the provision giving greater privacy protection controls.

sections.name: Preemption
sections.description: The title preempts local laws on the collection and sale of consumers' personal information.

sections.name: Regulations
sections.description: Rulemaking for the title, including cybersecurity audits, risk assessments and automated decision-making technology.

sections.name: Anti-avoidance
sections.description: Steps or transactions intended to avoid the title are disregarded.

sections.name: Waiver
sections.description: Contract provisions that waive or limit consumer rights under the title are void.

sections.name: Liberal construction
sections.description: The title shall be liberally construed to effectuate its purposes.

sections.name: Relationship to federal and state law
sections.description: The title supplements federal and state law where permissible and does not apply where preempted.

sections.name: Operative date
sections.description: The title became operative on January 1, 2020, subject to listed limitations.

sections.name: Operative date of Section 1798.180
sections.description: Section 1798.180 is operative on the effective date of the act adding this section.

sections.name: California Privacy Protection Agency established
sections.description: Creates the CPPA with full administrative power to implement and enforce the CCPA, governed by a five-member board.

sections.name: Qualifications and duties of agency board members
sections.description: Board members need privacy and technology expertise and must maintain confidentiality.

sections.name: Board member terms
sections.description: Members serve at the pleasure of their appointing authority for no longer than eight consecutive years.

sections.name: Board member compensation
sections.description: Per-day compensation and reimbursement of expenses for official duties.

sections.name: Executive director and staff
sections.description: The board appoints an executive director; the agency appoints officers, counsel and employees.

sections.name: Delegation of authority
sections.description: The board may delegate authority to the chairperson or executive director, except enforcement resolution and rulemaking.

sections.name: Functions of the agency
sections.description: Administer, implement and enforce the title, adopt regulations, promote awareness and cooperate with other authorities.

sections.name: Investigations
sections.description: The agency may investigate possible violations upon a sworn complaint or on its own initiative.

sections.name: Notice before a probable cause finding
sections.description: The business must be given notice and an opportunity to be heard at least 30 days before probable cause is considered.

sections.name: Hearings, orders and administrative fines
sections.description: After a hearing the agency may issue cease-and-desist orders and fines of up to $2,500 or $7,500 per violation.

sections.name: Rejection of an administrative law judge's decision
sections.description: The agency must state in writing its reasons for rejecting an ALJ decision.

sections.name: Subpoena powers
sections.description: The agency may subpoena witnesses, take evidence and require production of records.

sections.name: Five-year limitation period
sections.description: Administrative actions must be commenced within five years of the violation.

sections.name: Civil action to collect unpaid fines
sections.description: The agency may sue in superior court to collect unpaid administrative fines.

sections.name: Judgment to enforce a final order
sections.description: The agency may apply for a court judgment to enforce a final order or decision.

sections.name: Judicial review
sections.description: Agency decisions on complaints or fines are subject to judicial review for abuse of discretion.

sections.name: Civil penalties in actions by the Attorney General
sections.description: Injunctions and civil penalties of up to $2,500 per violation, or $7,500 if intentional or involving minors.

sections.name: Agency funding and inflation adjustments
sections.description: Appropriations for the agency and periodic adjustment of monetary thresholds and penalties.

sections.name: Consideration of good faith cooperation
sections.description: The agency and courts consider good-faith cooperation when deciding the amount of a fine or penalty.

sections.name: Service provider / contractor due diligence
sections.description: Regulations requiring businesses to exercise due diligence over service providers and contractors.
